title: Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.34167v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-using language model agents are usually evaluated by whether they finish the user's task. That metric misses a common failure: an agent can complete the requested work while also taking an unauthorized side-effecting action, such as writing to the wrong object, expanding the scope of the request, or contacting an unintended recipient. We call this failure mode collateral damage (CD). We introduce SABench (Side-effect-Aware Benchmark), a benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks. Each task crosses one of four state structures (independent, dependent, externally reachable, cross-tool) with one of four trap families (ambiguity, mis-targeting, cascade harm, overreach), and each task has a deterministic trace-based oracle for both goal satisfaction and authorization compliance. Across 2,211 model-task pairs from 11 frontier LLMs spanning major commercial and open model families, 15.2% of all runs incur CD, with risk concentrated

translated_title: 任务成功还不够：面向工具使用型语言模型代理的副作用感知评估
translated_abstract: 工具使用型语言模型代理通常以是否完成用户任务来评估。这一指标遗漏了一种常见的失败情形：代理可能在完成所请求工作的同时，还执行了未经授权的具有副作用的操作，例如写入错误的对象、扩大请求的范围，或联系非预期的接收者。我们将这种失败模式称为“附带损害”。我们提出了SABench（副作用感知基准），这是一个包含201个电子邮件、日历和工单任务的基准。每个任务将四种状态结构（独立、依赖、外部可达、跨工具）之一与四种陷阱类型（歧义、目标错位、级联伤害、过度扩权）之一相结合，且每个任务都配有一个确定性的、基于轨迹的判定器，可同时检验目标达成与授权合规性。在来自11个前沿大语言模型（涵盖主要商业和开源模型家族）的2,211个模型-任务对中，15.2%的运行产生了附带损害，且风险集中于……
tldr: 该论文提出SABench基准，首次系统性评估工具使用型大语言模型代理在成功完成任务时可能产生的未经授权副作用（“附带损害”），发现11个前沿模型中15.2%的运行存在此类风险。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces SABench, a side-effect-aware benchmark that systematically evaluates tool-using LLM agents for "collateral damage"—unauthorized side-effecting actions taken while completing tasks—finding that 15.2% of runs across 11 frontier models incur such failures despite task success.
